hamburg_eurogate_centre_location.title: Location & Route

callout.text: Walking is not recommended — pedestrian movement in the Waltershof port area is severely restricted and unsafe due to heavy container-truck traffic. Use the club shuttle.

hamburg_eurogate_centre_location.note: Avoid walking along Zellmannstraße and Finkenwerder Straße — both carry heavy traffic. Take the Duckdalben minivan or port transport/taxi instead.

hamburg_eurogate_transport_taxi.title: Taxi
hamburg_eurogate_transport_taxi.note: ~€35–45 to Landungsbrücken/Hauptbahnhof. Official German taxis are ivory/beige with an illuminated "TAXI" roof sign and a taxameter — anyone without that isn't licensed. Always ask for the taxameter to be switched on. Pay in EUR, card accepted.

callout.text: Never exchange money on the street, even for a good rate someone offers you — it's one of the most common ways seafarers get scammed near a port.

rows.title: A stranger offers you a better rate
rows.sub: On the street, at the gate, or "just around the corner" — always a scam

rows.title: Being asked to go somewhere private
rows.sub: A car, a back room, an alley — a legitimate exchange never needs this

rows.title: No receipt offered
rows.sub: A real exchange always gives you a printed receipt with the rate used

rows.title: Know the rough official rate first
rows.sub: Check on your phone before you go — so you can spot a bad deal immediately

rows.title: Count what you receive, before you walk away
rows.sub: In front of the person who gave it to you, not after
